column11: CMS Medicare Part D 2024, which the book already carries for Gardasil 9 (drug_demand, asset 389, part D, year 2024): $3,399,001.40 over 8,243 beneficiaries = $412.35 a beneficiary a year. The same row gives 11,989 claims, 1.45 a beneficiary, and 6,349.55 dosage units, 0.53 mL a claim, so a claim is one 0.5 mL dose at $283.51. Scale against the openly published list: the CDC vaccine price lists for 2026 put GARDASIL 9, NDC 00006-4121-02, 10 pack of 1 dose syringes, at $329.090 a dose private sector
column12: the line's only CMS series: quadrivalent Gardasil has no Part D row, and Medicare is a small adult corner of a vaccine given mostly to adolescents. It prices nothing in this file, since the one layer below is already approved, and is written so the asset carries a price when a real layer arrives. The CDC figures were read from the lists' text as a web search indexes them; cdc.gov could not be opened from this environment

column11: measured between two published prices, as gsk_arexvy.csv does: the CDC Pediatric/VFC Vaccine Price List of 1 January 2026 sets GARDASIL 9 (NDC 00006-4121-02) at a CDC cost of $257.071 a dose, contract to 2026-03-31, against the $283.51 a dose the CMS Part D 2024 row above implies. 1 - 257.071 / 283.51 = 0.0933
column12: a Part D anchor, so CMS spending is gross of rebates and a real deduction applies. The paediatric contract is taken because the line's revenue is mostly adolescent. The range is wide: the CDC adult list of 23 January 2026 puts the federal contract at $190.999 a dose, which gives 0.3263, and list to paediatric contract is 0.2188. This is the shallow end, so the row is not conservative

column10: share of the stock a year
column11: measured on the same beneficiaries as the price row, by the method the brief sets: 11,989 claims over 8,243 beneficiaries is 1.4544 doses a beneficiary in the year (drug_demand, asset 389, Part D 2024), against the label's three-dose course for ages 15 through 45 at 0, 2 and 6 months (GARDASIL 9 prescribing information, DailyMed setid a21f4f4b-b891-4f25-b747-cb9ec7d865d6, section 2.1), so a beneficiary takes 0.4848 of a labelled course in a calendar year and 1 - 0.4848 = 0.5152
column12: not a persistence measure, and pfe_prevnar.csv and gsk_arexvy.csv write 1.0 for a one-off course instead. The difference: paired with a per-beneficiary price, this rate puts $412.35 / 0.5152 = $800 on a vaccinee over their stay, 2.8 doses at the per-claim cost, which is about a completed course; 1.0 with the same price would count 1.45 doses and stop. The label section was not opened from here (DailyMed could not be reached); the schedule is the one the label has carried since 2016. Revisit if ACIP moves adults to a single dose

column10: share of the pool already in the base
column11: already approved: all three dated studies sit inside the population GARDASIL 9 is labelled for, girls and women 9 through 45 and boys and men 9 through 45 (DailyMed setid a21f4f4b-b891-4f25-b747-cb9ec7d865d6, version 31, July 2026, section 1, as the book's labels table holds it). NCT04199689 (V503-049, 6,033 men aged 20 to 45, persistent oral HPV infection, primary completion 2027-01-15) is the confirmatory study for the oropharyngeal and head and neck cancer indication the label already carries under accelerated approval. NCT07785843 (V503-108, 930 Chinese females 10 to 45 previously given a bivalent vaccine, immunogenicity, 2027-12-18) and NCT03998254 (V503-023, 6,000 Chinese women 20 to 45, efficacy against quadrivalent Gardasil, 2028-03-31) are Chinese studies in ages the label covers
column12: nil, not pending. A positive V503-049 converts an accelerated approval and adds no one the reported revenue does not already contain; a negative one puts the head and neck claim, not the vaccine's sales, at risk.
